title: The churches — one Lord, many traditions, calibrated
body: Every major tradition of the Church, gathered from its own confession and measured against the one plumb-line: Scripture in the original tongues and the ecumenical creeds. We calibrate, we do not judge — each tradition has kept a seed well; we name the gift and the ground held in common (Ephesians 4:4-6: one body, one Spirit, one Lord, one faith).
subject: the churches

connections.evidence: the traditions of the one Church, rooted in the Word

author: engine

title: The ecumenical creeds — the shared ground
body: The ecumenical creeds — the shared ground. Confession: Apostles' Creed; Nicene Creed (325/381); Chalcedon (451). Central emphasis: the Trinity, the incarnation, the death and resurrection of Christ, the one holy catholic Church. The seed it has kept: the core every tradition below confesses together — the center that holds. Anchored on: Matthew 28:19; 1 Corinthians 15:3-4; John 1:1-14. (Calibrated against the one plumb-line — Scripture in the original tongues and the ecumenical creeds — not judged; a tradition's gift, gathered.)

title: Eastern Orthodoxy
body: Eastern Orthodoxy. Confession: the Nicene Creed (without the filioque); the Seven Ecumenical Councils. Central emphasis: the unbroken worship and doctrine of the ancient Church; theosis — union with God; the mystery of the liturgy. The seed it has kept: continuity with the undivided Church and a deep reverence before the mystery of God. Anchored on: John 17:21-23; 2 Peter 1:4; Psalm 46:10. (Calibrated against the one plumb-line — Scripture in the original tongues and the ecumenical creeds — not judged; a tradition's gift, gathered.)

title: Roman Catholicism
body: Roman Catholicism. Confession: the Nicene Creed; the Council of Trent; the Catechism of the Catholic Church. Central emphasis: the visible unity of the Church, the sacraments, the communion of saints across time. The seed it has kept: a global, historic body holding the faith through the centuries with sacramental seriousness. Anchored on: Matthew 16:18; 1 Corinthians 11:23-26; 1 Timothy 3:15. (Calibrated against the one plumb-line — Scripture in the original tongues and the ecumenical creeds — not judged; a tradition's gift, gathered.)

title: Lutheran
body: Lutheran. Confession: the Augsburg Confession (1530); the Book of Concord; Luther's Catechisms. Central emphasis: justification by grace alone through faith alone; law and gospel rightly divided; the Word and the sacraments. The seed it has kept: the recovery of grace — that we are saved by Christ's work received, not our own achieved. Anchored on: Romans 3:28; Ephesians 2:8-9; Galatians 2:16. (Calibrated against the one plumb-line — Scripture in the original tongues and the ecumenical creeds — not judged; a tradition's gift, gathered.)

title: Reformed / Presbyterian
body: Reformed / Presbyterian. Confession: the Westminster Confession (1646); the Heidelberg Catechism; the Belgic Confession. Central emphasis: the sovereignty of God over all; covenant; Scripture as supreme authority; the whole life to God's glory. The seed it has kept: a God-centered vision of all things, and Scripture as the plumb-line over every claim. Anchored on: Romans 11:36; Ephesians 1:4-11; 2 Timothy 3:16-17. (Calibrated against the one plumb-line — Scripture in the original tongues and the ecumenical creeds — not judged; a tradition's gift, gathered.)

title: Anglican
body: Anglican. Confession: the Thirty-Nine Articles (1571); the Book of Common Prayer. Central emphasis: the via media — Scripture, tradition and reason; common prayer that forms a people. The seed it has kept: worship that catechizes, and a breadth that holds the reformed and the ancient together. Anchored on: Acts 2:42; Colossians 3:16; 1 Corinthians 14:40. (Calibrated against the one plumb-line — Scripture in the original tongues and the ecumenical creeds — not judged; a tradition's gift, gathered.)

title: Baptist
body: Baptist. Confession: the Second London Baptist Confession (1689); the New Hampshire Confession. Central emphasis: believer's baptism by immersion; the gathered church of the regenerate; the authority of Scripture; religious liberty. The seed it has kept: a personal, confessed, deliberate faith — and freedom of conscience before God. Anchored on: Acts 2:38-41; Romans 6:3-4; Matthew 28:19-20. (Calibrated against the one plumb-line — Scripture in the original tongues and the ecumenical creeds — not judged; a tradition's gift, gathered.)

title: Methodist / Wesleyan
body: Methodist / Wesleyan. Confession: the Articles of Religion (Wesley); the Standard Sermons. Central emphasis: grace freely offered to all; the new birth; sanctification — real holiness of heart and life. The seed it has kept: the pursuit of holiness and the reach of grace to every person, including the poor. Anchored on: Titus 2:11-12; Hebrews 12:14; 1 Thessalonians 5:23. (Calibrated against the one plumb-line — Scripture in the original tongues and the ecumenical creeds — not judged; a tradition's gift, gathered.)

title: Pentecostal / Charismatic
body: Pentecostal / Charismatic. Confession: the Statement of Fundamental Truths; the ancient creeds. Central emphasis: the present work of the Holy Spirit; the gifts; expectant prayer and worship. The seed it has kept: a living expectation that the Spirit still moves, heals and empowers today. Anchored on: Acts 2:1-4; 1 Corinthians 12:4-11; Joel 2:28. (Calibrated against the one plumb-line — Scripture in the original tongues and the ecumenical creeds — not judged; a tradition's gift, gathered.)

title: Anabaptist
body: Anabaptist. Confession: the Schleitheim Confession (1527); the Dordrecht Confession. Central emphasis: discipleship as the shape of faith; the peace of Christ; a community set apart from the world's coercion. The seed it has kept: the seriousness of following Jesus in daily life, and the ethic of peace and community. Anchored on: Matthew 5:1-12; John 13:34-35; Romans 12:1-2. (Calibrated against the one plumb-line — Scripture in the original tongues and the ecumenical creeds — not judged; a tradition's gift, gathered.)

title: Congregational / Free Church
body: Congregational / Free Church. Confession: the Savoy Declaration (1658); the Cambridge Platform. Central emphasis: the local congregation gathered under Christ's headship; the priesthood of all believers. The seed it has kept: the dignity and responsibility of the local body, ruled by Christ through his people. Anchored on: Matthew 18:20; 1 Peter 2:9; Acts 14:23. (Calibrated against the one plumb-line — Scripture in the original tongues and the ecumenical creeds — not judged; a tradition's gift, gathered.)
